knee osteoar- thritis is associated with deviations in gait patterns and performance-based measures and that the severity of these deviations is associated with patient-reported outcomes.
the overall gait deviations were significantly associated with pain, physical function, and performance-based measures.

1) the gait pattern of symptomatic knee OA patients is characterized by a reduced step length and increased double support time, and a reduced range of motion in knee and ankle joints during stance phase, 2) these deviations are more pronounced during walking than during overground running and are associated with worse physical functioning and worse self-reported knee pain, 3) the gait deviations are not related to age, BMI, or radiographic severity of OA.
